title: Missing second body off the ship's orbit plane: direction-dependent signature in 3D
description: Newtonian binary whose plane is tilted against the ship's orbit plane; the model knows only A. After distance calibration the misfit remains as tangential and orbit-normal (non-central) empirical acceleration that follows B's tidal field. Adding B (seen mode, six state parameters) restores chi2/nu = 1 and recovers mu.B and B's position, z included. Without any fix on B (unseen mode) its position is identifiable only locally, with mass and distance nearly degenerate.
units: SI: m, s, m/s, m/s^2, rad. A fix is [azimuth, elevation(, range)] of the inertial direction ship -> target: azimuth = atan2(d_y, d_x) in (-pi, pi], elevation = asin(d_z / |d|). sigma is per component; sigma_az carries the 1 / cos(elevation) of an isotropic pointing error. Attitudes are unit quaternions [w, x, y, z], body to inertial. Accelerometer samples are [f_x, f_y, f_z] in the body frame.
frame: Right-handed inertial. Gauge: body A at the origin and at rest at t = 0 of every attempt (spec 3.4). Body frame: +x forward, +y left, +z up.

propagation.note: Reference setting; all times are multiples of dt. Any propagator whose position error over the arc is below ~1 m reproduces the expected values.

tolerance.numeric: Fits with compare = numeric: |x_impl - x_ref| <= 0.05 sigma_ref per parameter; |sigma_impl / sigma_ref - 1| <= 0.05; |chi2_impl / chi2_ref - 1| <= 0.02; |rho_impl - rho_ref| <= 0.02. Tier L windows: same boundaries (t0, t1, nFixes) and |g_impl - g_ref| <= 0.05 sigma_ref. Profile nodes: |g_impl - g_ref| <= 0.1 sigma_ref.
tolerance.qualitative: Fits with compare = qualitative are grossly misfitted (chi2/nu > 25) or unconverged; only the inequalities in `checks` and any heldOut.pass value are required.
tolerance.physicalClaims: Per check, stated in `checks`. The generator refuses to write a vector whose claims fail.

notes: Fit `add-body-B-unseen` uses the fixes on A only (`dataSubset`) and is solved without arc growing (`solver`). Its `farStart` block is a development record, not an expected value.
`truth` blocks are for checking only and must never reach the estimator (P11). Measurements whose target is not a modelled body are ignored by that fit.
Covariances of positions are [xx, xy, xz, yy, yz, zz].

attempts.note: Newtonian binary (B at 4 r0, binary plane inclined 25 deg). Ship coasts around A, r 0.8-1.2 r0 (16 h), in a plane inclined 70 deg. Fixes on A every 180 s, on B every 600 s.

fits.description: Newtonian model with A only; B's gravity is not modelled and B fixes are ignored.
Diagnostic: A-only reference law (main-fit values) times the calibration profile, plus radial / tangential / orbit-normal empirical acceleration per window (frame body A).
Unmodelled-body extension, seen mode: B's 6-state from its fixes, mu.B fitted (prior mean 0, sigma 1e11).

Unmodelled-body extension, unseen mode: B's six state numbers and mu.B from the ship's motion alone (no fix on B). Local identifiability only: started 5% too far along the true direction with mu.B 20% low, and solved on the whole arc at once.

solver.note: No arc growing (spec 4.5): on a quarter of the arc the unseen body is not determined and runs away.

farStart.note: Not a claim and not an expected value. The same fit started 20% too far and 0.2 rad off in direction with mu.B = 1.5e9: the plain solver creeps along the mu / d^3 valley. The search of spec 6.3 (and a better parameterization) is still to be built and tested.

windowRule.label: ASSUMED
windowRule.source: Tier L: a window closes after the bearing sweeps 0.7 rad (40 deg) or ln(range) spans 0.15, with at least 12 fixes. Scale-free, so independent of the 1B scale.
